correctness.rationale: The reduction to the greedy Mersenne Apéry weight w(j)=j+c(j), nondecreasing for 0<=j<a, identifies the maximum from the final constant-weight plateau. The binary splitting criterion yields c(M)=2t and plateau length delta+1 for M=m2^n. The maximal residue a-(delta+1) produces F=M²+a(2t-1)+delta. The proposed formula also has an exact independent cross-check against the previously proved all-parameter greedy formula: for h=2..199, computing greedy Mersenne coin count c_h and smallest occupied index i_h gives h+c_h=2t and i_h-1=delta. Thus the old formula M²+(h+c_h-1)M+(h+c_h+i_h-2) agrees term for term with the assigned expression. The proof handles n>=3, odd m>=3 and m<2^n, including h=7 and unbounded delta.
residual_risks: Independent 199-weight check is finite; the source proof derives the all-weight splitting property, and previous published theorem already establishes all parameters.
Full Dijkstra residue-graph check from source script was inspected, not independently rerun for all 119 cases.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Let M=m2^n, h=popcount(m), c=number of greedy coins in h, i=lowest occupied greedy coin index. Earlier theorem F=M²+(h+c-1)M+(h+c+i-2). In the new parametrization h+c=2t, i=delta+1, giving F=M²+(M+1)(2t-1)+delta exactly. The identity is structural, not a search-keyword match.

originality.rationale: An earlier complete all-odd-parameter Proth Frobenius formula (published 2026-10-25) covers precisely this semigroup and every n>=3, odd 3<=m<2^n. The assigned formula is an algebraic reparameterization of that theorem: the new t corresponds to half the prior h+c and delta to the prior least greedy index minus one. Thus the claimed formerly untreated all-weight cases had already been resolved.
residual_risks: No ambiguity remains about mathematical coverage; any questions about original implementation choices do not restore novelty of the claimed Frobenius formula.

value.rationale: The all-parameter Proth Frobenius problem is valuable, but its exact closed formula and unique maximizer had already appeared in the October 25 published result. Recasting the same answer as a minimum binary-weight index and unbounded correction is a change of notation, not substantive new information.

final_claim: For every n>=3 and odd 3<=m<2^n, the Proth semigroup Frobenius number equals (m2^n)^2+(m2^n+1)(2t-1)+delta with h=popcount(m), t=min{v>=1:2v-popcount(v)>=h}, delta=h-(2(t-1)-popcount(t-1))-1, including the unbounded-correction families.
limitations: Rejection is for exact prior coverage, not false numerical computation.
